newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea ruling party will not debate strike leader.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea ruling party will not debate strike leader.

text.p: South Korea's ruling New Korea Party on Friday turned down a debate with the country's top strike leader over a controversial new labour law.

A party statement ruled out debate with "people who have legal problems". A warrant has been issued for the arrest of the head of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, Kwon Young-kil, who earlier said he was ready for a televised debate with the ruling party chairman.

"Even for a television debate, the law should be observed," the statement quoted party spokesman Kim Chul as saying. "There cannot be guarantees of safety for people who have legal problems due to arrest warrants."
But he welcomed what he called the acceptance in principle by the confederation of a televised debate.
Kwon had insisted any debate must be between himself and ruling party chairman Lee Hong-koo. He stipulated it should be live and the government must guarantee his security from arrest.
The spokesman urged the confederation to put forward candidates for a debate who had no legal complications and said the debate could be aired live.
